empathy.justification: The model demonstrates excellent empathy, acknowledging the importance of the gift, the frustration of the missed deadline, and the customer's specific stress regarding having something for their dad to open.
quotes: I completely understand. With only two days left, wanting something certain for him to open makes sense.
I'm sorry your dad's gift is stuck, especially with his birthday so close.

resolution_quality.justification: The model provides clear, actionable options that directly address the customer's dilemma. It thoroughly explains the trace vs cancel options and gives a great, practical breakdown of what happens if they cancel but the item arrives later.
quotes: If having a gift in hand on the day matters most, cancelling and buying something you can get locally is the surest route.
Just reply with **"keep and trace"** or **"cancel."**
Keep the order in transit instead of cancelling. You'd still get the $12 express fee back, and the puzzle would be yours whenever it arrives.

policy_honesty.justification: The model perfectly adhered to all policy constraints. It was clear about the refund math, the sold-out status, the timing of refunds, and explicitly stated that no actions had been taken yet. It also handled an off-policy question (what happens if I keep a cancelled item) by honestly stating the policy doesn't cover it rather than hallucinating an answer.
quotes: The $12 express fee is included in the $76, so there's no separate or additional fee refund on top of it.
Our policy doesn't spell out what happens if a cancelled parcel is kept instead of returned. I don't want to guess about charges or other outcomes, so I'd rather not promise anything either way.
Nothing has been changed on your order yet.

overall_impression: An exceptional response. The agent handled a high-stress situation with perfect clarity, excellent empathy, and strict adherence to policy, including navigating an edge-case question flawlessly.
